name: Commerce
description: Trade and the aids to trade — production, home and foreign trade, business units, finance, transport, insurance and the Nigerian commercial environment — aligned to WAEC, NECO and JAMB Commerce.

topics.name: Introduction to Commerce
topics.summary: What commerce is, how it sits inside production, and the occupations it creates.

subtopics.name: Meaning and Scope
subtopics.summary: Commerce as trade plus the aids to trade, and why it matters in Nigeria.

objectives.text: Define commerce and distinguish it from trade and from industry
Draw the structure of commerce: home trade, foreign trade and the aids to trade
State the functions of commerce in an economy

subtopics.name: Occupation
subtopics.summary: Industrial, commercial and service occupations, and factors that influence choice of occupation.

objectives.text: Classify occupations as industrial, commercial or services
Give Nigerian examples of each class of occupation
Explain factors that influence a person's choice of occupation

subtopics.name: Production
subtopics.summary: Primary, secondary and tertiary production, and the factors of production.

objectives.text: Define production and state when production is complete
Distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary production with examples
Name the factors of production and the reward of each

topics.name: Home Trade
topics.summary: Wholesale and retail trade inside Nigeria, and the documents that move with the goods.

subtopics.name: Wholesale Trade
subtopics.summary: The wholesaler as the link between manufacturer and retailer.

objectives.text: Define a wholesaler and state types of wholesaler
Explain the services a wholesaler renders to the manufacturer and to the retailer
Discuss reasons for the decline of the independent wholesaler

subtopics.name: Retail Trade
subtopics.summary: Small shops, supermarkets, department stores, hawking and e-retailing.

objectives.text: Define retailing and list types of retailer in Nigeria
Compare a supermarket with a department store and a hawker
State the recent trends in retailing, including e-commerce

subtopics.name: Documents of Trade
subtopics.summary: Enquiry, quotation, order, invoice, delivery note, debit and credit notes, and receipt.

objectives.text: List the documents used in a home-trade transaction in order
State the purpose of an invoice, a delivery note and a credit note
Interpret trade discount and cash discount on an invoice

topics.name: Foreign Trade
topics.summary: Import, export and entrepôt trade, procedures, and the documents and payments that make it work.

subtopics.name: Nature of Foreign Trade
subtopics.summary: Why countries trade, and the difference between visible and invisible trade.

objectives.text: Define foreign trade and distinguish import, export and entrepôt trade
Distinguish visible from invisible trade and define the balance of trade and of payments
State advantages and disadvantages of foreign trade for Nigeria

subtopics.name: Barriers and Procedures
subtopics.summary: Tariffs, quotas, customs, and the steps in importing and exporting.

objectives.text: Explain tariffs, quotas, embargoes and foreign-exchange control
Outline the procedure for importing goods into Nigeria
Outline the procedure for exporting goods from Nigeria

subtopics.name: Documents and Payments
subtopics.summary: Bill of lading, certificate of origin, letter of credit and other tools of foreign trade.

objectives.text: State the purpose of a bill of lading, certificate of origin, consular invoice and insurance certificate
Explain a letter of credit and a bill of exchange
Identify incoterms such as FOB and CIF in outline

topics.name: Aids to Trade
topics.summary: Transport, communication, warehousing, insurance, banking and advertising.

subtopics.name: Transport and Communication
subtopics.summary: How goods and messages move, and why each mode is chosen.

objectives.text: State the functions of transport in commerce
Compare road, rail, water, air and pipeline transport in Nigeria
Explain how communication aids trade

subtopics.name: Warehousing and Insurance
subtopics.summary: Holding stock safely, and spreading risk so trade can continue.

objectives.text: State the functions and types of warehouses
Define insurance and state the principles of insurance
Distinguish life, fire, marine, motor and fidelity-guarantee insurance

subtopics.name: Banking and Advertising
subtopics.summary: How banks and advertisements oil the wheels of trade.

objectives.text: State the commercial functions of the Central Bank and of commercial banks
Explain a cheque, a standing order and a bank draft
State the functions, types and media of advertising

topics.name: Business Units
topics.summary: From the sole proprietor to the public corporation — who owns the firm and who bears the risk.

subtopics.name: Sole Proprietor and Partnership
subtopics.summary: The smallest units, their advantages, and why many Nigerian firms start here.

objectives.text: State the features, merits and demerits of a sole proprietorship
State the features of a partnership and the contents of a partnership deed
Explain unlimited liability and why it matters

subtopics.name: Limited Companies
subtopics.summary: Private and public companies, shares and the idea of limited liability.

objectives.text: Distinguish a private from a public limited company
Explain limited liability, shares and debentures
Outline how a company is formed (memorandum and articles)

subtopics.name: Public Enterprises and Cooperatives
subtopics.summary: Government-owned businesses and cooperative societies.

objectives.text: State reasons for public enterprises and give Nigerian examples
Explain privatisation and commercialisation
State the features and types of cooperative societies

topics.name: Finance and Capital
topics.summary: Where a business gets its money, and the institutions that supply it.

subtopics.name: Business Capital
subtopics.summary: Fixed, circulating, owned and borrowed capital, and the capital market.

objectives.text: Distinguish fixed from circulating capital, and owned from borrowed capital
Calculate working capital
State sources of short-term and long-term finance

subtopics.name: Money and the Stock Exchange
subtopics.summary: Functions of money, and how the Nigerian Exchange helps firms raise capital.

objectives.text: State the functions and qualities of money
Explain the functions of the stock exchange
Distinguish a share from a debenture and a bull from a bear

subtopics.name: Credit
subtopics.summary: Trade credit, hire purchase, deferred payment and the risks of selling on credit.

objectives.text: Define credit and state types of credit used in trade
Compare hire purchase with deferred payment
State advantages and risks of granting credit

topics.name: The Consumer and the Market
topics.summary: Protecting the buyer, and the organised markets where commodities are traded.

subtopics.name: Consumer Protection
subtopics.summary: Why the buyer needs protection, and the agencies that provide it in Nigeria.

objectives.text: State reasons for consumer protection
Name Nigerian consumer-protection agencies and their roles (FCCPC, SON, NAFDAC)
Outline the rights of a consumer

subtopics.name: Commodity and Produce Markets
subtopics.summary: Commodity exchanges, organised produce markets and the middlemen of Nigerian trade.

objectives.text: Define a commodity market and give examples relevant to Nigeria
Explain the functions of middlemen in produce trade
State the aims of a commodity exchange

subtopics.name: E-commerce
subtopics.summary: Buying and selling online, and what it changes for Nigerian traders.

objectives.text: Define e-commerce and give Nigerian examples
State advantages and disadvantages of e-commerce
Outline the documents and payments used in online trade

topics.name: The Nigerian Commercial Environment
topics.summary: The setting in which Nigerian businesses actually operate.

subtopics.name: The Business Environment
subtopics.summary: Political, legal, economic, socio-cultural and technological influences on a firm.

objectives.text: List the components of the business environment
Explain how government policy can help or hinder commerce
Give Nigerian examples of environmental influence on a firm

subtopics.name: Economic Groupings
subtopics.summary: ECOWAS, the AU and other groupings that shape Nigerian trade.

objectives.text: State the aims of ECOWAS and of the African Union in trade
Explain how a customs union differs from a free-trade area
Discuss benefits and problems of regional economic integration

subtopics.name: Customs and Excise
subtopics.summary: The agencies that collect duty and police the border.

objectives.text: State the functions of the Nigeria Customs Service
Distinguish customs duty from excise duty
Explain why smuggling harms legitimate commerce
